newsitem.title: USA: Best cuts American Eagle Insurance rating.
newsitem.headline: Best cuts American Eagle Insurance rating.

text.p: A.M. Best said that it lowered American Eagle Insurance Co of Dallas to "D" or poor from its vulnerable "B" or fair rating.
Best said its action reflects its view that American Eagle's weakened financial condition makes it "extremely vulnearble" to unfavorable changes in underwriting or economic conditions.
It said it was also concerned over potential regulatory response to the position of American Eagle, whose capitalization, it said, had fallen below mandatory control level of risk-based capital.
Best said its downgrade was based on the "substantial deterioration" of American Eagle's financial condition and follows a $45.7 million net loss for 1996.

The loss is based on statutory accounting rules and is different from Monday's $44.4 million net loss reported by American Eagle as its net loss for 1996, which is in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) basis, according to a Best analyst tracking the company.

The loss included an unexpected $30 million fourth-quarter charge for reserve additions and reinsurance costs related to discontinued businesses and continuing core aviation operations, it said. As a result, the company's 1996 statutory surplus plunged 60 percent from the previous year's level, it said.
The company is extremely leveraged, Best added, with $110.1 million of net written premiums and $73.0 million of year-end loss reserves supported by $20.4 million in surplus, it added.
Best also noted that American Financial Group Inc Inc would not pursue an alliance with American Eagle that would have stabilized the company's financial condition.
Best noted that American Eagle was pursing capital and strategic alternatives, which may include the sale of the company or its assets, a rights offering to shareholders or an offering of securities.
Best said it will continue to monitor the company's financial condition, which may be subject to further loss-reserve development or potential regulatory moves.
